clue.text: Stay calm, and don't get shown up?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for not losing your temper
second meaning, read literally: someone who keeps their top on is not exposed to view

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: a person who stays clothed is not shown up in the sense of being revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to remain composed and not lose one's temper, while its literal sense is staying dressed.

clue.text: Peck biography includes old film's first revival

indicators.note: the first pair of words holds the next letters within them

parts.note: a peck is a quick kiss
a biography is a life story, a 'life'

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: only its first letter is used, as the clue says

explanation.surface: A biography of the actor Gregory Peck that covers the revival of an old film.
explanation.walkthrough: Peck looks like the Hollywood star; here it is a light kiss. The letters for 'old' and the film's first letter sit between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouth-to-mouth resuscitation, which brings someone back from apparent death, is a figurative revival.

clue.text: Undermining eastern nation, spy who takes up residence?

indicators.note: in a down entry the nation's word sits beneath, or undermines, the eastern letter

parts.note: a state is a nation
an agent is a spy

explanation.surface: An enemy agent working against an eastern country while living there undercover.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: this person takes up homes in the sense of handling them for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A property professional deals in houses, taking on people's residences to market and sell them.

clue.text: Talks over food and drink

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
rations are allotted supplies of food and drink

explanation.surface: Discussions held across a meal and drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal speeches delivered to an audience are talks in the plural noun sense.

clue.text: Wife leaving fizzy wine, happy in festival

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling agitation, so the letters are churned into a new order
the letter for wife departs from the word wine

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife gives up sparkling wine but stays cheerful during the holiday season.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast on 6 January marks the visit of the Magi, a church festival.

clue.text: All there in possession of this?

definitions.meaning: the idiom for being mentally sound, not missing anything upstairs
the quality one must have to be described that way

explanation.walkthrough: Someone who is 'all there' has their wits about them, which is exactly the quality asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness of mind is what being 'all there' means, so the person possesses mental health.

clue.text: Design trendy outlet

parts.note: in means fashionable
a vent is an outlet for air or steam

explanation.surface: Planning a fashionable shop or outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise something new is to design it, as a verb.

clue.text: Seaman in goal, first half only

indicators.note: only the opening half of the six-letter word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: a target is a goal

explanation.surface: A sailor plays in goal but only for the opening half of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A tar is old slang for a sailor.

clue.text: Those opposed to sound of a hooter

indicators.note: says that the answer is heard like the word that follows

parts.note: hooter is slang for a nose

explanation.surface: People who object to the noise a car horn makes.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooter looks like a horn; it is slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: In a vote, the people saying no are the noes, those who oppose the motion.

clue.text: Flying to Tunisia for ball game

indicators.note: flying letters are scattered and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Travelling by air to Tunisia to watch or play a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: From the idiom 'a whole new ball game', meaning a changed set of circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball game is informal American usage for a state of affairs or set of circumstances.

clue.text: Edge shown by abrupt church official

indicators.note: abrupt means cut short, so the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a verger looks after a church interior

explanation.surface: A brusque church attendant shows irritation or edginess.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is the border or margin of something, its edge.

clue.text: Bird in hosta, scratching wings and rolling in it

indicators.note: the outer letters, the word's wings, are scratched out

parts.note: a hosta is a leafy garden plant; taken as written
the idiom for being very wealthy

explanation.surface: A bird in a hosta bed, scratching about and rolling around in the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Wings suggests the bird, but here means the two end letters of the plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless African runner is a species of bird.

clue.text: Romantic present

definitions.meaning: second meaning, a verb: to offer formally

explanation.walkthrough: Present reads as a gift or the current time; it is the verb to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both loving and gentle, and to submit or offer something formally.

clue.text: Short cable tie's entangled with rubber loop

indicators.note: entangled things are twisted together, so the letters are jumbled
the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
the plural of tie, read as written
and can mean along with

explanation.surface: A brief bit of cable used as a tie is tangled up with a rubber band.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretchy ring used to hold things together is a loop made of rubber.

clue.text: Mean to accompany film star Mae from Utah to Kentucky?

parts.note: a mean is a middle or average point
Mae West was the Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: A nasty character accompanies Mae West on a tour across the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean looks like an adjective for unkind; it is the noun for an average.
explanation.definitionFit: The central region of the United States is loosely bounded by states such as Utah and Kentucky, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Left netting in study

parts.note: netting money is earning it

explanation.surface: Someone who left the nets, or fishing, to take up study.
explanation.walkthrough: Netting suggests mesh, but here means making a net profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is the acquisition of knowledge through study, both as a noun.

clue.text: Load one minicab, possibly

parts.note: to tax is to burden or load
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Pack the luggage into a single minicab, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: A minicab is a British private-hire car booked by phone, a type of cab.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicab is one example of a hired car for passengers, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Colourful flier on the front of Yarmouth Empire

parts.note: the monarch is a bright orange butterfly

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: a town on the Norfolk coast; taken as written

explanation.surface: A colourful aircraft flies over the seafront of Yarmouth's Empire theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Flier suggests a plane or pilot; it is a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm ruled by a sovereign is a kingdom, and an empire is one such state.

clue.text: Rep loath to travel too much?

indicators.note: the letters move about and settle in new places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sales rep reluctant to do too much travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or overabundance; the question mark admits a noun for an adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Loud where drivers begin reversing for some distance

indicators.note: the golf word is turned back to front

parts.note: golfers drive off from the tee at each hole

explanation.surface: Noisy motorists start backing up for a fair way down the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Drivers here are golfers, or golf clubs, not motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet are units of length, so a number of them is a measured distance.

clue.text: Arranged neckband right away — tweed, oddly

indicators.note: the letter for right goes away from the word

parts.note: a collar is a band round the neck

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions are taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tweaked a tweed collar, removing the right-hand part in an odd way.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate is to gather and put in order, so collated means put in sequence.

clue.text: Paper to settle up with woman

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to sit is to settle down
Sue is a woman's name, a common crossword source of letters

explanation.surface: A paperwork deal to settle a debt with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle up suggests paying a bill; the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a thin, soft kind of paper.

clue.text: The cad fights divorce

indicators.note: fighting letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bounder of a husband fights his wife's divorce petition.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce something is to separate it, the verb sense of disconnect.

clue.text: Sit-down buffet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sit-down is one kind of industrial action
second meaning, a verb: to hit or knock

explanation.walkthrough: Sit-down buffet suggests a seated meal, but buffet is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a walkout by workers and a blow or hit.

clue.text: For example, The Thing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 'the' is the definite ... in grammar
second meaning: an item or object

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest a film title, The Thing; split it so 'the' is the grammatical example.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls 'the' and 'a' by this name, and the word also means an item or object.

clue.text: Clubs for raving

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sticks for hitting a ball, as in cricket
second meaning: mad, informal for crazy

explanation.walkthrough: Clubs for raving suggests nightclubs; the word means both sticks and crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for hitting implements and informal slang meaning mad.

clue.text: Covering head, modifies house

indicators.note: the first letter is covered over, hidden from view

parts.note: varies means changes or modifies

explanation.surface: Putting a roof over the top changes the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In astrology the zodiac signs are houses, and this is the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ram is a sign of the zodiac, which astrologers call a house.

clue.text: Hotel's apron missing outside

indicators.note: the outer letters are missing

parts.note: a pinny, short for pinafore, is an apron

explanation.surface: A hotel's apron is nowhere to be found outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a small hotel or public house offering lodging.

clue.text: Get on with television presenter in US city

parts.note: a news anchor presents on television
to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: Getting along with a TV presenter in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of Alaska is an American city.

clue.text: Noticed Yes and Heart playing for a long time

indicators.note: the band names are played around with into new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spotted the rock bands Yes and Heart performing over a long career.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means from a very long time ago, for ages.
